source: Objective (the user 2026-10-13): the cheapest lane that still gets great results, judged per finished task, and fluid with Claude's quota pace. Evidence: audit 2026-10-12 + Theo t3 stance as of 2026-10-12: Opus 5.5 is Theo's default for judgment work; never max; Opus 5.5 xhigh scores 56.0 vs 53.6 on high (slopalytics 2026-10-08, both on the cost frontier) and Theo runs Opus on xhigh themselves (video ND_kRgU_WlY 42:39); low and Sonnet 5.5 not worth it; Haiku 5.5 only for fan-outs where most attempts are wasted; Fable for marketing pages and big design overhauls; since Sol 6.1 (2026-09-29) Theo pairs Opus with GPT-6.1 Sol day to day; OpenAI models review Claude's code (cross-lab review).

claude.subagent.role: Opus high for routed judgment work (feature-build, research-synthesis, computer-use); no env default, every dispatch names its model

claude.judge.role: critic / verify stages a workflow author opts into

claude.deep.role: hard engineering: ports, large refactors, deep debugging, architecture

claude.sweep.role: optional: pure extraction fan-outs where most attempts are wasted (workflow author opts in)

claude.design.role: marketing pages and big design overhauls only, by deliberate pick

claude.distill.role: handoff-v2 session distiller (primary); local.text is the fallback

codex.check.role: code review and checks (cx check); cross-lab reviewer of Claude's code

codex.vision.role: bulk image classification in headless pipelines (reasoning low)

local.text.role: handoff distiller fallback and lane auto:local

routes._how: Every dispatch (Agent, Workflow agent, cx, claude -p, lane) names one task class below and uses its lane; there is no default, and the route-guard hook denies an Agent or Workflow agent() call that names no model. A route's optional alt lane (Codex) takes the job while Claude's weekly use runs ahead of the week (route.py reads the live usage records). `route list` shows the table, `route <class>` prints how to dispatch it. Lanes say which model and effort; routes say which lane fits which job.

interactive.why: Opus high: the user 2026-10-13 traded xhigh's +2.4 points for about half the cost per turn (claude.deep keeps xhigh for hard engineering)
interactive.source: the user 2026-10-13; slopalytics 2026-10-12 (high 53.6 at $1.82, xhigh 56.0 at $3.46)

feature-build.use: a normal multi-file code change in a repo, frontend or backend
feature-build.why: Opus 5.5 is Theo's build model; high sits on the cost frontier

hard-engineering.use: ports, large refactors, deep debugging, architecture, or anything a first attempt got wrong
hard-engineering.why: Opus on xhigh finished a port that OpenAI models topped out at 84% on

long-unattended-build.use: hours-long or high-volume builds that run without supervision (cx build)
long-unattended-build.why: Sol 6.1 tied Opus 5.5 on Terminal Bench at about 1/13 the cost; the user: Codex for long unattended runs

code-review.use: review a Claude-written diff before it merges (cx check); a high-stakes diff also gets an Opus xhigh review
code-review.why: cross-lab review: Sol catches the dumb things Opus misses and is Theo's preferred reviewer, but Sol alone finds less

plan-review.use: adversarial review of a plan, design doc or finished batch (cx plan read-only); a high-stakes plan (auth, secrets, schema, migrations, payments, public exposure) also gets an Opus xhigh pass (claude.deep)
plan-review.why: bake-off 2026-10-18 (blind Opus and Sol judges): Astra xhigh and Sol 6.1 xhigh tied, both follow instructions; Theo's Astra complaints are about building and obeying edits, not read-only review, so the lane stays. Opus xhigh found the most defects but bundles and pads, so it is the second pass, not the first

security-review.use: public-push gate reviews, exposure audits, history sanitization; exposure audits and history rewrites also get an Opus xhigh second reviewer (claude.deep); the guard gate's automated Codex step is unchanged
security-review.why: the user: Codex owns the GitHub-security heavy lifting; Astra xhigh finds real defects and tied Sol in the 2026-10-18 bake-off; one reviewer alone misses things (Theo)

ui-design.use: marketing pages and big visual overhauls only
ui-design.why: the user's rule; Theo uses Fable for screenshot-to-UI. Theo also says Fable is off the frontier for general work, so nothing else routes here

research-synthesis.use: multi-source research that needs judgment and a written conclusion

bulk-sweep.use: reading many docs or pages for specific facts, extraction or classification over many items, fan-outs where most attempts are wasted
bulk-sweep.why: Theo: reading docs for facts is when Haiku is incredible; more attempts beat smart attempts there

code-search.use: finding where something lives or how it flows across many files when only the conclusion matters (Explore agent)
code-search.why: keeps the parent's context small: rereading a long context is most of the Opus spend (cache reads); Haiku reads for facts well

bulk-vision.use: classifying many images in a headless pipeline
bulk-vision.why: Theo: for vision, Luna, because it is cheaper with reasoning off

verify-judge.use: critic and verify stages inside a workflow
verify-judge.why: xhigh beats high on hard judgment and never max

session-distill.why: a blind judge scored it well above the local model, a few cents a session

headless-summary.why: judgment over a week of evidence

computer-use.use: driving the identity browser or desktop apps (web skill, computer-use MCP)
computer-use.why: those tools exist only on Claude's side on odin; Theo prefers Astra for computer use, but Codex's sandbox cannot drive the browser

private-data.use: anything with PII or private content that must stay on thor (lane auto:local)
private-data.why: the user's rule: private or PII stays on thor

not_routed.claude-sonnet-5-5: dominated: Opus 5.5 high scores higher for less (53.6 at $1.82 vs Sonnet xhigh 51.9 at $2.01); Theo: skip Sonnet, use Opus and Haiku (video 38_6C0dkKmU 37:45)
not_routed.gpt-6-luna for code: Theo: anyone who thought Luna was decent at code, question their judgment (video 38_6C0dkKmU 09:35); Luna is routed for bulk vision only
not_routed.Muse Wonder Full (Meta): unreachable on our subscriptions or $0 routes: no API, only in Meta's paid Muse Code plans (Power $50/mo or Maximum $200/mo; Theo: video DbWL6Zs2j_g 03:35, NE006pkiAnk 10:38); not on OpenRouter or FreeLLMAPI (checked 2026-10-27, both list only the API model meta/muse-wonder at $4/$20 per M, which Theo calls not worth its price, video DbWL6Zs2j_g 25:25)
not_routed.trivial lookups: no dispatch: a grep or one-file read is done inline

rules: cheapest lane that still gets great results, judged per finished task, not per token (the user 2026-10-13; Theo video vRS2leJLAI0); Opus only where a cheaper lane misses the bar, xhigh only for verify stages and hard engineering

fluid with quota: while Claude's weekly use runs ahead of the week (or the 5-hour window is at 80%+), a route's alt lane takes the job; route.py decides live from the usage records, nobody sets a default
every Agent and Workflow agent() call names its model (route-guard hook); there is no CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL fallback
max only where it is the cheapest lane that passes a bar xhigh missed; today none (Theo 2026-09-25: xhigh beats max on Opus 5.5; slopalytics 2026-10-12: max +1.6 points for 1.7x the cost)
cross-lab review: Claude writes, a Codex model reviews
triage every review finding against the task's scope before acting; reject overengineering and scope creep, most of all from a cross-family reviewer (Theo video hiI0Vk4NgeY 35:17)

a high-stakes diff or plan (auth, secrets, schema, migrations, payments, deletes, public exposure) gets a second reviewer from the other family, never Sol alone (Theo video DbWL6Zs2j_g 29:29; bakeoff-2026-10-18)
a lane change must name its source (video id, post id, or slopalytics snapshot date) in history
